comments.text: Born and raised in BC and love it.  But I hate how much logging that has gone on in its history.  So much of the provinces forests are 'fake' forests, or tree farms, which ruined its ecology.  I get it, you need to show the good stuff for the purposes of this video, but BC is slowly degrading due to over population and environmental destruction, forest fires and what not.  I bet in 100 years, BC will look like Europe.  'Forests' will be small patches of trees, nothing like it is today.  It will be raw mountain grasslands.  So record/take pictures while we can.  Like the rest of the world.  Its over soon.

comments.text: 🏔🌲 British Columbia is one of Canada's most breathtaking regions, where vast wilderness, towering mountains, ancient forests, and remote communities reveal a world far beyond modern civilization! ❤ Is anyone currently living in British Columbia watching this documentary, and what is everyday life really like in this beautiful and wild part of Canada?

replies.author: @stevedockeray
replies.text: Lived here since 1967 & it just becomes the place we live you get used to it - but you get reminded by vids like this . Worked as a commercial salmon  fisher & traveled & fished from the Fraser River around Vancouver Island & up the coast  almost to  the Alaskan border . Places like Rivers Inlet ( a Fjord like in Norway ) on the upper coast where there was no radio TV or roads touches you deep inside and stays . This was 1986 & even today you have to fly or boat in as there are no roads ( there are small forest service roads in the area but no way to drive there ) .

replies.author: @gregelden8611
replies.text: Living in Kelowna, I have been blessed to experience about 90% of these places. I can't imagine living anywhere other than British Columbia. After half a century, I still wonder at the beauty of this place.

replies.author: @J.Lesley-l4c
replies.text: Kind of normal. Work, eat, sleep, surf the net and watch TV. A lot of places are inaccessible unless you are a hard core hiker, the rest are touristy, but nothing like as busy as Europe.  You do have to be aware of bears and cougars if you go hiking. Even so, life is very different to Europe for example, where every inch of land is measured and owned by someone. Access to lakes and boat launches are free. It is important to remember it is wilderness and it is not difficult to get lost and die out there, so the freedom of the wilderness is limited by its dangers. You travel in hours not miles/ km, but it is nice to experience the world before concrete.
